entries.abstract: Formalization of incremental n × n Latin squares and cyclic incremental n × n Latin squares representing n + 1 solutions of (n, c)-coins problems simultaneously for all 0 ≤ c ≤ n. We prove that (1) for every n ≥ 4, any incremental n × n Latin square represents valid (n, c)-coins solutions for all 0 ≤ c ≤ n simultaneously via value thresholding, and (2) for every n ≥ 4 with n ∉ {4, 6}, there exists a column permutation p such that the cyclic Latin square L(i, j) = (i + p(j)) mod n is incremental, using an injective-majorization principle across four infinite modular families modulo 6 and the four exceptional dimensions n ∈ {8, 9, 15, 21}, together with explicit non-cyclic incremental Latin squares for n = 4 and n = 6.
entries.title: Cyclic n × n Latin Squares Representing Solutions of (n, c)-Coins Problems

entries.abstract: Explicit one-tape, two-symbol Turing machines with a designated beep state (Aaronson's beeping busy beaver convention), given as literal transition tables, together with core-Lean proofs (no Mathlib) that each machine, run from the blank tape, beeps only finitely often exactly when a stated Sigma_2 sentence holds. The flagship machine (278 states) is equivalent to the Sigma_2 form of P = NP: some candidate program decides a fixed self-padded NP-complete language within a polynomial clock on every instance. The equivalence of that sentence with P = NP is also proved in Lean (ZP.Cx.sentence_iff_PeqNP) for the Turing-machine models defined in the development. The same guest interpreter yields machines for further Sigma_2 statements: P = PP and P = PSPACE, factoring, discrete logarithm, graph isomorphism, an NTT-based variant over least primes 1 + n i, linear-time integer multiplication on multitape machines, a co-NP verifier variant, promise-P = promise-BPP, NP in P/poly, deterministic and nondeterministic multihead log-space (L = NL), and linear-time multiplication of matrices over GF(2) on multitape machines. A 19-state machine quasihalts iff there are finitely many twin primes.
entries.title: A beeping busy beaver machine for the Σ₂ form of P vs NP

entries.abstract:
This Lean 4 and Mathlib development produces exact, machine-checked positivity certificates for finite Gram matrices built from Suzuki's zeta screw function. Weil's explicit formula recasts the Riemann Hypothesis as positivity of a quadratic form assembled from prime powers, and a recent line of work truncates that form and studies the resulting finite matrices. The objects formalized here are the screw function Psi, defined as an archimedean profile minus a von Mangoldt weighted prime sum and extended evenly; its Gram kernel G(t,u) = Psi(t) + Psi(u) - Psi(t-u); and positive definiteness, in the quadratic-form sense, of the finite matrices this kernel generates on explicit grids.
The three compared results are as follows. (1) On the grid (0.2, 0.4, 0.6) the 3 by 3 Gram matrix M3 of the genuine kernel satisfies an explicit Rayleigh floor: for every real vector x, 0.005 times the sum of the x_i squared is at most the quadratic form of M3 at x. (2) M3 is positive definite. (3) On the grid (0.4, 0.9) the 2 by 2 Gram matrix is positive definite. The prime sum in Psi vanishes for t below log 2 (about 0.693) and the node 0.9 lies above it, so the p = 2 prime term contributes to this matrix.
The interest is that the surrounding literature (Connes and van Suijlekom; Connes, Consani and Moscovici; Suzuki) works either in floating point or at the level of existence statements, whereas these are exact certificates checked against the definition of Psi itself. Suzuki establishes that some positivity window exists; here an explicit one is exhibited, with an explicit margin, and verified, to our knowledge for the first time.
Scope is finite and explicit. Every positivity statement concerns a specified grid at specified rational nodes; there is no asymptotic, fine-mesh or all-grid result; and nothing here bears on the Riemann Hypothesis.
entries.title: Certified Positivity: machine-checked positivity windows for the Suzuki zeta screw kernel

entries.abstract: We prove in Lean that infinitely many primes p have Ω(p − 2) odd, where Ω counts prime factors with multiplicity, giving an affirmative answer to Green's Problem 64. The argument constructs a nonnegative weight supported on odd prime-factor parity; correlation estimates and a weighted sieve give positive total weight to integers u with u + 2 prime at arbitrarily large scales. The supporting analytic number theory is included in the formalization, with Mathlib as its only direct dependency.
entries.title: Green's Problem 64: odd prime-factor parity in shifted primes

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Darboux's theorem in the form Kim Morrison stated it for lean-eval (problem darboux): if a 2-form on an open set U of R^2n is smooth, closed and non-degenerate, then every point of U has a neighbourhood with a smooth chart, smooth in both directions, in which the form takes the standard values on the standard basis, so it is the standard symplectic form sum dx_i ^ dx_(n+i). The proof is Moser's: interpolate between the form and its value at the point, write the difference as d(beta) by a Poincare lemma, integrate the vector field X_t with i_(X_t) omega_t = -beta to time 1, and get a chart from the inverse function theorem; a symplectic basis of the form at the point then gives the standard coordinates. Mathlib has no symplectic forms and no Darboux theorem. When lean-eval posed the problem in May 2026 it found no formalization in any proof assistant; since then three other Lean proofs of Darboux's theorem have appeared, each with its own statement (listed under related_formalizations). This proof is independent of them. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed.
entries.title: Darboux's theorem: every symplectic form on an open subset of R^2n is locally the standard one

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the paper Pretorsion theories and image-closed subcategories, in two parts. Structure: for a finite-dimensional algebra Λ over a field, a subcategory Z of mod Λ is image-closed iff Z = Gen Z ∩ Cogen Z iff Z = T ∩ F for a pretorsion theory (T, F) (Theorem A), and the pretorsion theories of mod Λ form a complete lattice with the meets and joins of the paper (Theorem 3.6). Enumeration: for the linearly oriented quiver 1 → ⋯ → n, the pretorsion theories, weighted by q to the number of indecomposables in T ∩ F, and the image-closed subcategories, weighted by q to their number of indecomposables, sum to the q-Gandhi polynomials B_{n+1}(1, q) and C_{n+1}(1, q) of Han and Zeng (Theorem B), with the two-variable refinements of Theorems 7.5 and 8.5. At q = 1 these are the Genocchi numbers g_{2n+4} and the median Genocchi numbers H_{2n+3}; that classical evaluation is not formalized. The library also proves the other numbered statements of the paper, including the convex geometry of image closure (Section 4.3), and the cited inputs they use.
entries.title: Pretorsion theories and image-closed subcategories

entries.abstract: Closed forms for det[(i−j)^m + δ_ij]_{1<=i,j<=n}: m = 1 (A079034; Wang–Sun 2022), and Zhi-Wei Sun's conjectured formulas for m = 2 (A355175) and m = 3 (A355326, Conjecture 1), proved by Fried (2026).
entries.title: Sun's determinants det[(i−j)^m + δ_ij] for m = 1, 2, 3

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that there is an 8-regular simple graph of girth 7 on 768 vertices (Mathlib's SimpleGraph, IsRegularOfDegree and girth), so that the order n(8, 7) of an (8, 7)-cage is at most 768; the House of Graphs cage table listed 774 when this was written. The graph is data (adjacency lists in a binary trie). Lean's kernel checks (decide +kernel, no native_decide) that it is simple and 8-regular, and, for every vertex v and every two neighbours x ≠ y, that the ends of the non-backtracking walks of length at most 3 starting with the edge v x are disjoint from those starting with v y. A cycle of length at most 6 would contradict this at one of its vertices, and an explicit 7-cycle gives girth exactly 7.
entries.title: An 8-regular graph of girth 7 on 768 vertices

entries.abstract: For every prime p, p | M(p−2) iff p ≡ 1 (mod 3), and M(p−2) ≡ −1 (mod p) when p ≡ 5 (mod 6). Conjectured by Serge Batalov (2022) for p ≡ 1 (mod 6); proved by Rob Burns (2017) and Nadav Kohen (2024).
entries.title: OEIS A001006: Motzkin numbers at p − 2 modulo p (Batalov's conjecture; Burns, Kohen)

entries.abstract: For A(x) = Σ a(n) x^n/n! with A(x) = x exp(A∘A∘A∘A(x)), every a(n) (n >= 1) is an integer not congruent to 3 mod 5. Conjectured by Paul D. Hanna; an informal proof is in Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt report (2026). The Lean proof is different.
entries.title: OEIS A396804: a(n) mod 5 is never 3 (Hanna's conjecture)

entries.abstract: Two graphs on the same n vertices pack if 2 Δ(G1) Δ(G2) < n (Sauer and Spencer 1978).
entries.title: The Sauer–Spencer packing theorem

entries.abstract: If Σ a(n) x^n/n! = F(x) exp(x G(x)) with F, G integer power series and G(0) = 1, then a(n+k) ≡ a(n) (mod k) for all n, k (Bala 2017, Theorem 1). Hence A000262 (exp(x/(1−x))) and A082579 (exp(x/(1−x)^2)) satisfy k | a(n+k) − a(n) for k >= 2.
entries.title: OEIS A000262 and A082579: Bala's Theorem 1 (periodicity modulo every k)

entries.abstract: For a finite set A of complex numbers, the multiset of k-element subset sums together with |A| determines A when |A| is divisible by a prime p > k, and when k = 4 and |A| > 12 (Selfridge–Straus 1958).
entries.title: Erdős Problem 494: Selfridge–Straus, A is determined by its k-sums when |A| has a prime factor p > k, and when k = 4, |A| > 12

entries.abstract: Three classical reconstruction theorems: a disconnected graph on at least three vertices is determined by its vertex deck (Kelly 1957); a graph with m > C(n,2)/2 edges (Lovász 1972) or with n! < 2^(m−1) (Müller 1977) is determined by its edge deck.
entries.title: Graph reconstruction: disconnected graphs (Kelly) and the Lovász and Müller edge bounds

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the matrix multiplication tensor ⟨9, 11, 11⟩ has rank at most 708 over the rationals. Two compared theorems: 708 triples of rational matrices decompose the tensor (∑ᵢ uᵢ[a, b] vᵢ[c, d] wᵢ[e, f] = [b = c ∧ a = e ∧ d = f]), and the same triples form a bilinear algorithm A * B = ∑ᵢ (∑ uᵢ[a, b] A[a, b]) (∑ vᵢ[c, d] B[c, d]) wᵢ over every field of characteristic zero. The scheme, scaled to integers, is data; Lean's kernel checks it (decide +kernel, no native_decide) slice by slice with the coefficients packed into large integers, and a soundness proof for every input turns the 99 slice checks, a range check and a bound check into the tensor identity. The smallest rank listed for this format in the Lille catalogue was 710 when this was written.
entries.title: Multiplying 9 × 11 by 11 × 11 matrices with 708 multiplications

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the matrix multiplication tensor ⟨9, 10, 11⟩ has rank at most 640 over the rationals. Two compared theorems: 640 triples of rational matrices decompose the tensor (∑ᵢ uᵢ[a, b] vᵢ[c, d] wᵢ[e, f] = [b = c ∧ a = e ∧ d = f]), and the same triples form a bilinear algorithm A * B = ∑ᵢ (∑ uᵢ[a, b] A[a, b]) (∑ vᵢ[c, d] B[c, d]) wᵢ over every field of characteristic zero. The scheme, scaled to integers, is data; Lean's kernel checks it (decide +kernel, no native_decide) slice by slice with the coefficients packed into large integers, and a soundness proof for every input turns the 90 slice checks, a range check and a bound check into the tensor identity. The smallest rank listed for this format in the Lille catalogue was 644 when this was written.
entries.title: Multiplying 9 × 10 by 10 × 11 matrices with 640 multiplications

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of special transformations and RV lifting in algebraically closed valued fields of pure characteristic zero. The first Comparator configuration selects Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 5.6: special-bijection deformation to RV-pullbacks and preparation of polynomial RV values. Genuine saturation and a small original parameter set are explicit. Jacobian and measured-lifting results remain in the larger verified library but are outside this first submission claim.
entries.title: Special transformations in algebraically closed valued fields

entries.abstract: For all natural numbers q and m, exp(Σ_{n>=1} q^(n^m) x^n/n) is a power series with integer coefficients. Conjectured by Paul D. Hanna (2009) and proved by Sela Fried (2025).
entries.title: OEIS A158110: exp(Σ q^(n^m) x^n/n) has integer coefficients (Hanna's conjecture, Fried 2025)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem of Narayanan, Vasudevan and Somasundaram (arXiv:2610.16258) that every finite elementary graph satisfies ch(G) = χ(G) = ω(G) (chromaticChoosable_of_isElementary; clique number at most k implies k-choosability for every colour type, choosable_of_isElementary), together with the structure theorem of Maffray and Reed (JCTB 75, 1999, Theorem 2, (i) ⇒ (iii)) that the proof starts from: every finite elementary graph is an augmentation of the line graph of a bipartite multigraph, given by an explicit edge representation (rep_of_isElementary; IsAugLineGraphRep: vertex v is the edge {a v, b v} of a bipartite multigraph; non-adjacent pairs sharing an end share exactly one end, which is a hub with at most two neighbours; no edge joins two hubs). The earlier statements for the representation class are kept (choosable_of_rep, chromaticChoosable_of_rep, isElementary_of_rep, rep_of_lineGraph, rep_of_cobipartite). The choosability proof follows the paper (Hall, the Deficiency Lemma, saturation, Proposition 3.7, Galvin; Kőnig avoided). The Maffray–Reed proof follows the paper's induction by compression of strong homogeneous pairs (growth procedure from an induced D, claims (1)–(2), A-components, Theorem 5), with every forbidden-subgraph step done as a parity argument on a fixed elementary colouring; Theorems 3–4 are replaced by a "bend" lemma, and two exposition gaps of the paper (p. 143 and Case 3 of claim (2)) are repaired. Galvin's theorem for bipartite multigraphs is imported as a lake dependency from PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000029 v2.
entries.title: Elementary graphs are chromatic-choosable

entries.abstract: For a finite family of differentiable convex beta-smooth losses with a population minimizer, this formalization proves an expected last-iterate population-loss bound for stochastic gradient descent under uniform sampling with replacement and uniform sampling without replacement. With delta = min(1, 2 - eta beta), the bound is 280000 times log(T+2)^3 / log(2+log(T+2)) times [R^2 / (delta^3 eta T) + eta sigma_star^2 / delta^4]. It holds for all 0 < eta beta < 2, every positive WR horizon, and every WOR horizon through one full pass, including T = n. Under interpolation at eta = 1/beta, this yields O(beta R^2 log(T)^3 / (T log log(T))). The two compared theorems use the actual finite sampling averages and the usual SGD recursion. All history estimates and stochastic sampling identities are proved from the stated assumptions.
entries.title: Improved last-iterate bounds for SGD with and without replacement

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about R^n with a diagonal metric eta whose entries are +1 or -1 (every signature). A covector field omega is conformal Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 2 phi eta_ij for some function phi, and Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 0. (1) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields are exactly the members of an explicit family: translations, rotations (an antisymmetric matrix), the dilation and the special conformal fields. (2) In every dimension the Killing fields are exactly the affine fields a + A x with A antisymmetric. (3) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension (n+1)(n+2)/2. (4) In every dimension the Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension n(n+1)/2. (5) A control for the hypothesis n >= 3 of (1): in the Euclidean plane there is a conformal Killing field that is not a member of the family for any values of its parameters, the matrix being any real matrix, antisymmetric or not (the witness in the proof is the real and imaginary parts of z^3). Statements (6)-(9) are statements about conserved currents: they say which fields give conserved currents. (6) If a tensor field T and a covector field omega are differentiable at a point x, T(x) is symmetric and the conformal Killing equation holds at x with factor phi, then the current J^i = sum_j T^ij omega_j satisfies div J = (div T) . omega + phi tr_eta T at x. (7) A C^3 field is conformal Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free, eta-trace-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (8) A C^3 field is Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (9) For n >= 1 the dilation omega_j = eta_j x_j is conformal Killing and is not Killing. The Challenge imports Mathlib only and carries the definitions its statements use (the partial derivative, the two equations, the family, the two solution spaces as submodules, the divergences, the current and the metric trace), each with its convention. Statements (1)-(4) are classical: (1) and (3) are the classification of the conformal Killing fields of R^{p,q}, p + q >= 3, and the count of their parameters (Schottenloher 2008, Theorem 1.7; Ginsparg 1988, section 1.1), the infinitesimal counterpart of Liouville's theorem on conformal maps; (2) and (4) are the Killing fields of flat space and their number. (6) is the standard identity behind the conserved currents of a trace-free stress tensor, and (5) and (9) are standard examples. In (7) and (8) the direction from the equation to conserved currents is (6); the other direction was not found stated in the sources read for this entry, is elementary (it is proved by testing on constant tensor fields, so it is a pointwise fact of linear algebra) and is not claimed as new. No statement is claimed as a new theorem. Scope: diagonal metrics with entries +1 or -1 (a general constant metric, reached by a linear change of coordinates, is not formalized); C^3 covector fields on all of R^n; the numbers in (3) and (4) are dimensions of real vector spaces, with no Lie bracket and no isomorphism with so(p+1,q+1) stated; the finite conformal maps (Liouville's theorem itself) are not formalized; nothing is said about compactly supported tensor fields in (7) and (8). Prior formalization, recorded under related_formalizations: the identity (6), with its corollary for conserved trace-free tensors, is formalized for n = 4 and signature (1,3), for tensors of tempered distributions, in github.com/openai/math; special cases of the currents are in the Yang-Mills release github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028 and in facebookresearch/atlas-lean, and Killing fields on Riemannian manifolds are in atlas-lean and in TauCetiProject/TauCeti. In a dated search no formalization was found of (1)-(5) or of the direction of (7) and (8) from conserved currents to the equation. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): for n = 4 and a Lorentzian signature the spaces of (3) and (4) have dimensions 15 and 10, the infinitesimal conformal symmetries and the infinitesimal isometries of Minkowski space, and (6) is the conservation law for the currents of a conserved symmetric stress tensor against them, trace-free in the conformal case.
entries.title: Conformal Killing and Killing fields of flat pseudo-Euclidean space: classification for n >= 3 in every signature, the two dimension counts, and the divergence of the current of a symmetric tensor field

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the scalar local limit theorem with corrected stable norming (Theorem 1.10), the admissible leaf counts and their probability asymptotics (Theorem 3.1, Introduction (I)), maximum degree concentration under the paper's hypothesis H (Theorem 7.1(ii)), and corrected probability asymptotics for the number of vertices with degree in an arbitrary set (Theorem 8.1(I)). The principal functional results are the joint convergence of the rescaled Lukasiewicz path, contour and height under leaf conditioning (Introduction (II), including lattice laws) and under offspring-mark conditioning (Theorem 8.1(II)). Nine principal declarations and their explicit construction lemmas are selected for comparison. Tree laws, codings and limit laws are concrete; evaluation and J1 metric instances are fixed by checked characterizations.
entries.title: Invariance principles for Galton–Watson trees conditioned on the number of leaves

entries.abstract: Quantitative Poisson approximation for long multiplicative runs requires arithmetic control uniform over growing subfamilies. The selected results give the exact affine event calculus, homogeneous and compatible-nullity envelopes, unique relation-respecting component factorization, and a weighted full-support count summed over all cardinalities with one threshold before every subset and minimum size; actual positive Hermite reference laws with an exact-parameter N^(-4/3+epsilon) upper error bound and fixed-height sharp moving total-variation equivalents; and an explicit counterexample showing that agreement at every fixed factorial-moment order, even with uniform exponential-moment control, does not imply any inverse-power total-variation rate. The quadratic positivity interval and singleton identity calibrate the positive-reference family. The counterexample is an independently constructed family of probability laws; no multiplicative realization is asserted. The selected conjunctions cover main results 2.1--2.5, 7.1 and 8.4 and companion Propositions13.1 and15.1, including the latter's displayed sequence corollary.
entries.title: P1: uniform event calculus, Hermite laws and the fixed-moment obstruction

entries.abstract: The partition number p(n) is even for infinitely many n and odd for infinitely many n (Kolberg 1959). The proof uses Euler's pentagonal number theorem over F_2.
entries.title: Kolberg's theorem: the partition function takes each parity infinitely often

entries.abstract: For every n, 2^(n(n+3)) divides the (n+1)×(n+1) Hankel determinant det[a(i+j)] of the Catalan–Larcombe–French numbers a, and the quotient is a positive odd integer. This is Zhi-Wei Sun's conjecture (2013), proved by Zhu and Sun (2018).
entries.title: OEIS A053175: Hankel determinants of the Catalan–Larcombe–French numbers

entries.abstract: Every finite simple graph without an isolated edge has edge weights in {1,...,5} such that adjacent vertices have different weighted degrees (Kalkowski, Karoński and Pfender 2010). The {1,...,30} bound of Addario-Berry et al. (2007) follows as a corollary. The 1-2-3 conjecture itself (Karoński, Łuczak and Thomason 2004), with weights {1, 2, 3}, was later proved by Keusch (2024); this entry formalizes the earlier {1,...,5} theorem, not Keusch's proof.
entries.title: The 1-2-3 conjecture with weights 1..5 (Kalkowski–Karoński–Pfender)

entries.abstract: The ordinary generating function A(x) of OEIS A396843, with A(0) = 0 and A'(0) = 1, satisfies A(x A(x) − 3x A(x)^2) = x^2. The package proves that this equation has exactly one integer power-series solution and that every term a(n) with n ≥ 1 is odd, as conjectured by Paul D. Hanna (OEIS A396843, 2026). An earlier Lean proof of the oddness is in the-omega-institute/trureturing PR #6773.
entries.title: OEIS A396843: integral construction and oddness (Hanna's conjecture)

entries.abstract: Let F(n) be the maximal length of a 2-increasing sequence of triples in {1..n}^3, where a triple is 2-less than another if it is smaller in at least two coordinates. Gowers and Long show that F(n) ≥ n^{3/2} when n is a perfect square (arXiv:1609.08688, Proposition 1.4). The package proves (√n)^3 ≤ F(n) for every perfect square n.
entries.title: Gowers–Long: F(n) ≥ n^{3/2} when n is a perfect square

entries.abstract: TxGraffiti Conjecture 2 asserts Z(G) ≤ α(G) + 1 for every connected graph G of maximum degree at most 3 other than K4, where Z is the zero forcing number and α the independence number (recorded by Davila, Brimkov and Pepper, arXiv:2507.17780). Mikko Fischer found a connected 24-vertex counterexample (arXiv:2607.23664). The package certifies that Fischer's graph is connected, has maximum degree 3, zero forcing number at least 11 and independence number at most 9.
entries.title: TxGraffiti Conjecture 2 is false (Fischer's counterexample)

entries.abstract: The exponential generating function A(x) of OEIS A368630 satisfies A(0) = 1 and A(x/A(x)^2) = exp(x A(x)). The package proves that this equation determines a unique integer coefficient sequence, and that a(n) ≡ 1 (mod 3) for every n, a(2n) is odd for every n, and a(2n+1) is even for n ≥ 1, as conjectured by Paul D. Hanna (OEIS A368630, 2024).
entries.title: OEIS A368630: three congruences (Hanna's conjectures)

entries.abstract: Conjecture 291 of DeLaViña's Written on the Wall II says that every connected graph on more than two vertices satisfies γ_t(G) ≤ k + f, where γ_t is the total domination number, k the first Havel–Hakimi step at which a zero appears, and f the number of vertices lying in the fewest triangles. The package certifies a 12-vertex counterexample with γ_t = 4, k = 2 and f = 1: the m = 6 member of a family posted by vulnix0x4. The source credits the disproof to Zyad Tamimi.
entries.title: WOWII Conjecture 291 is false (a 12-vertex counterexample)

entries.abstract:
This project proves the Reinhardt conjecture in Lean 4. Every centrally symmetric convex disk in the plane has greatest packing density at least that of the smoothed octagon, approximately 0.902414. The smoothed octagon is a regular octagon whose corners are replaced by arcs of hyperbolas. Equality holds precisely for its images under invertible affine maps.

The proof uses Hales's optimal control formulation and builds on the libraries lean4-smoothed-polygon and lean4-optimal-control. It also verifies the construction and packing density of the smoothed octagon.
entries.title: The Reinhardt conjecture, formalized in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the preprint "A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub- and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity" (J.-M. Mirebeau, Y. Mouheb, 2026). The preprint introduces the adaptive narrow band (ANB) method, which solves the fixed point problem Λu = u of a monotone, possibly non-causal, discretization Λ of a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman or Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, such as the anisotropic eikonal equation, up to a relative tolerance ε, by constructing a sub-solution and a super-solution. The compared theorems concern the algorithm meant to be implemented, the ANB with sorted lists: when the scheme is sub-additive in Kruzkov exponential coordinates, the fixed point exists, is unique and satisfies a comparison principle, and the algorithm terminates with a sub-solution and a super-solution within relative distance ε, after O(|ln ε|²) updates at each point uniformly in the discretization, with explicit bounds on the number of iterations, the width of the narrow band, the number of evaluations of the causal operator and the number of operations on the sorted lists. These bounds yield the quasi-linear complexity O(N |ln ε| ln(N/ε)) of the paper. The development proves all the lemmas, propositions and theorems of the preprint (151 statements), including the correctness of the generalized Dijkstra method with a stopping time and the equivalence of the ANB with its implementation by sorted lists.
entries.title: Complexity of the adaptive narrow band method for non-causal eikonal schemes

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Condensation in subcritical Cauchy Bienaymé trees (Kortchemski–Vetter, arXiv:2503.07530v2). For size-conditioned subcritical Bienaymé trees with offspring probabilities asymptotic to L(n)/n², where L is measurable and slowly varying, the development proves condensation of the maximal degree, the geometric depth of the condensation vertex, logarithmic tree height and its tightness criterion. It also proves the underlying one-big-jump principle by two routes, the stable limit, maximal-degree fluctuations and second-order height asymptotics. The development also proves the corrected five-case classification of heavy-tailed offspring laws up to Kennedy equivalence (exponential tilting), including critical and subcritical cases, under the necessary assumption of positive mass at zero. Four source statements are formalized in corrected form, with the corrections documented. Background assertions refuted by counterexamples and external citations are distinguished in the coverage report. The comparison interface contains twenty results whose proofs use only the three standard axioms.
entries.title: Condensation in subcritical Cauchy Bienaymé trees

entries.abstract: Exact expansion at the first excluded ordered prefix and a positive remainder kernel under arbitrary dependence. A universal heterogeneous Poisson–Charlier conversion bound is applied to the actual run model. Complete-law transfer explicitly assumes the 254 fixed-order connected-activity estimates; reconstruction from absolute triple activity and the resulting 4/3 upper bound are unconditional.
entries.title: P1 publication: Stopping and complete-law reconstruction

entries.abstract: An explicit binary Turing machine with 196 working states searches for a contradiction in ordinary first-order Peano arithmetic. Lean proves blank-tape nonhalting and that PA proves neither the exact arithmetic halting sentence nor its negation. A refutation compiler connects the PA proof predicate to the literal 392-row table. The axiom command uses a transposed quantifier code and a guarded equality-vacuity clause.
entries.title: Nonhalting and PA-independence for a 196-state Turing machine

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of quantifier elimination for algebraically closed fields, nontrivially valued algebraically closed fields in the ordinary valued-field language, and the corrected two-sorted RV language with named RV inversion. This Comparator configuration checks those three entry points. Only nontrivial valuations are included in the valued-field claims.
entries.title: Quantifier elimination for algebraically closed valued fields

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the Gallai–van der Waerden numbers GW(r; 3, 4) of Mao, Ozeki, Robertson and Wang equal 53 for r = 3, 4 and 5. GW(r; 3, l) is the least m such that for every n ≥ m, every exact r-colouring of {1, …, n} contains a rainbow 3-term or a monochromatic l-term arithmetic progression. Upper bound: for every r ≤ 5 and every n ≥ 53, every r-colouring of {1, …, n} has a rainbow 3-term or a monochromatic 4-term progression. This is reduced to the unsatisfiability of a CNF with 265 atoms and 43,562 clauses (colours renamed in order of first appearance), and the unsatisfiability is checked in Lean's kernel (decide +kernel, no native_decide) from an LRAT certificate of 1,211 derived clauses by a bitmask unit-propagation checker whose soundness is proved in Lean for every input. Lower bound: explicit exact 3-, 4- and 5-colourings of {1, …, 52} with neither progression, checked by the kernel. Together: GW(3; 3, 4) = GW(4; 3, 4) = GW(5; 3, 4) = 53.
entries.title: Exact Gallai–van der Waerden numbers: GW(r; 3, 4) = 53 for r = 3, 4, 5

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_2(G)/γ_3(G) has exponent at most 3, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group, γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) and γ_2(G)^9 ⊆ γ_4(G), and most generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) (paper, Theorems 6.6, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10 and 6.11), and whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite p-group, p odd, and [γ_2(G), γ_2(G)] ⊆ γ_5(G), in particular for finite metabelian 3-groups, which is Gupta–Tahara's theorem at p = 3 (paper, Theorem D.1; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7); the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 (Proposition 2.1); and a minimal counterexample is a candidate (Lemma 5.2). The proofs of the last two use D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem, all proved in the development (dThreeEqGammaThree, passiDFourSquare, gruenbergResidualTwo). One conditional result, with the assumption an explicit hypothesis: D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form, assuming Proposition 5.3). One compared result is not in the paper: D_5(Q) = 1 for every finite group Q of class at most 4 with Q/γ_2(Q) ≅ C_3 × C_9 × C_9, with no condition on γ_4(Q) (in particular for γ_4(Q) ≅ C_9, which the paper's Theorem 6.11 does not cover); its proof on paper is in the author's research notes (public account: docs/ab399.md), and the paper is not being changed to include it.
entries.title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib proofs that no directed strongly regular graph exists for 28 parameter sets (v, k, t, λ, μ). A directed strongly regular graph is a 0-1 matrix A with zero diagonal, all row and column sums equal to k and A² = tI + λA + μ(J − I − A). Nine of the parameter sets are those of the paper below: (50, 11, 7, 0, 3), (68, 13, 7, 0, 3), (100, 16, 7, 0, 3), (108, 19, 9, 0, 4), (55, 16, 12, 1, 6), (66, 10, 5, 4, 1), (91, 12, 6, 5, 1), (96, 15, 10, 9, 1) and (28, 6, 3, 2, 1); the tenth set of the paper, (48, 9, 5, 0, 2), is not formalized. The same lemmas exclude eight further sets, and a formalized complement lemma excludes eleven complementary sets. The proofs compare the rank of A − θI, for a root θ of the quadratic x² − (λ − μ)x − (t − μ), with a submatrix of A prescribed at one vertex. For (28, 6, 3, 2, 1) one case is a SAT refutation whose LRAT certificate the Lean kernel checks with decide +kernel. The theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Nonexistence of directed strongly regular graphs by rank arguments

entries.abstract: For every n and every primitive complex (2n+1)-th root of unity ζ, the permanent of the 2n × 2n matrix with entries 1 on the diagonal and (1 + ζ^(j−k))/(1 − ζ^(j−k)) off it equals 4^n (n!)^2/(2n+1). Zhi-Wei Sun posed the identity in OEIS A002454 (2022), and She, Sun and Xia proved it (arXiv:2208.12167, Theorem 1.3(ii)). The proof formalizes the determinant approach of Guo, Li, Tao and Wei.
entries.title: OEIS A002454: the odd-order permanent identity (She–Sun–Xia)

entries.abstract: M. J. Plantholt and S. Shan, Edge coloring graphs with large minimum degree (arXiv:2105.05286), in Lean 4 / Mathlib. theorem_1_2 (Theorem 1.2): for every ε > 0 there is N such that a graph G on 2n vertices, n ≥ N, with δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n is Δ(G)-edge-colourable iff it has no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (PlantholtShan.HasOverfullSubgraph, the definition of the registered plantholt-overfull-criterion entry restated in the challenge: an odd set of at least three vertices spanning more than Δ(G)(|S| − 1)/2 edges). theorem_1_3b (Theorem 1.3, Condition (b)): two vertices x ≠ y with d(x) = d(y) ≥ (1/2 + 3ε/2) n, all other vertices of degree Δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n and Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ (1/2 − ε/2) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N. theorem_1_3c (Condition (c)): Δ(G) − δ(G) ≥ n^{6/7}, at least n^{6/7} vertices of degree δ(G), at least n + 1 of degree Δ(G) and δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N (n^{6/7} as a real power). Condition (a) (regular graphs) is the registered asymptotic-one-factorization entry. lemma_2_11 (Lemma 2.11): a bipartite graph with sides of size n, all degrees at least t and at most t vertices of degree below n/2 has a perfect matching. Kept from version 1: hakimi (Theorem 2.5), hamiltonConnected_of_minDegree (Theorem 2.6, δ ≥ n/2 + 1) and exists_spanning_paths (Lemma 2.12). The thresholds N are explicit but huge (e.g. (2^60 q + 1)^21 with 1/q < ε) and not optimized. Two definitions (IsMultigraph, HasOverfullSubgraph). Seven statements.
entries.title: Plantholt–Shan: the overfull conjecture for graphs of minimum degree at least (1 + ε) n

entries.abstract: Positive and signed arithmetic profiles over ordered separated pairs of multiplicative runs, including both moving residue phases and the explicit two-channel probability law. Every fixed finite channel-height truncation has a literal next-height cumulant and law remainder and a sharp total-variation equivalent. Weighted nonaligned pairs, the closed height-five correction, and the height-six phase are included with their exact coefficients.
entries.title: P1 publication: Arithmetic pair profiles and finite channel heights

entries.abstract: Actual heterogeneous factorial-count identities, with repeated-index corrections, and the unconditional optimal 41/30 power for the third factorial cumulant. Absolute triple activity has the same upper exponent. The fourth-cumulant decomposition retains the positive compatible quartic mass and distinguishes 5/3 and 3/2 errors; the exact quadratic Poisson–Charlier approximation has matching 4/3 upper and lower power bounds.
entries.title: P1 publication: Factorial cumulants and optimal quadratic error

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 proof that Smale's mean value constant equals 4. For a complex polynomial p of degree d >= 2 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) != 0, let S(p) be the minimum of |p(c)/(c p'(0))| over the critical points c of p, let K(d) be the supremum of S(p) over all such p of degree d, and let K* be the supremum of K(d) over d >= 2. In 1981 Smale proved K* <= 4 and asked whether 4 can be replaced by 1 (and asked it again in 2000). The formalization proves K* = lim_{d -> oo} K(d) = 4, which is Theorem 1.1 of D. Goel, "Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4". It also proves Smale's bound K(d) <= 4, that K(d) does not decrease with d, and that K(d) < 4 for every d.
Comparison with Smale's conjecture. Smale asked whether K* = 1. That was disproved in 2026 (Adamczewski's Lean disproof; Adamczewski and Colbrook). Jatar and Ng then proved K* > 1.1018, and the author proved K* > 1.1559. This project does not prove the conjecture: it answers Smale's question in the negative. K* equals 4, Smale's own bound, so no constant smaller than 4 works for all degrees. In each single degree the constant stays below 4: K(d) <= 4^((d-2)/(d-1)) (Beardon, Minda and Ng, 2002), and K(d) < 4 - 2.263/sqrt(d) for d >= 8 (Crane, 2007). So the supremum K* is not attained.
entries.title: Smale's mean value constant equals 4

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the asymptotic form of the Chetwynd–Hilton 1-factorization conjecture (Perković and Reed 1997, Häggkvist): for every ε > 0 there is N such that every d-regular simple graph on 2n vertices with n ≥ N and d ≥ (1 + ε) n is 1-factorizable, i.e. its line graph is d-colourable (one_factorization); the integer form with (q + 1) n ≤ q d for q ≥ 1 is one_factorization_of_ge. The proof follows Vaughan (arXiv:1010.5192) for multiplicity 1: a balanced bipartition A, Aᶜ with |d_A(v) − d_{Aᶜ}(v)| < s for every vertex (Lemma 13, here by a counting Chernoff bound with no probability theory), equitable colourings of the two sides with matched class sizes (Vizing and McDiarmid's equalisation, from the registered Vizing entry), 5-edge alternating-path exchanges until every colour class is a perfect matching, completion of the classes of the leftover inside edges by Hall's theorem, and a decomposition of the remaining regular bipartite graph into perfect matchings (Hall). Vaughan's sizes n^{2/3} and n^{5/6} are replaced by linear sizes s = ⌊a/(200q)⌋ and t = ⌊a/6⌋ with a = ⌊n/q⌋; N is explicit, N = L (512 L³ + 4) with L = 200 q² for d ≥ (1 + 1/q) n (very large). No definitions beyond Mathlib's. Two statements.
entries.title: Asymptotic 1-factorization of dense regular graphs (Perković–Reed, via Vaughan)

entries.abstract: The full original run-count law has optimal quadratic Poisson–Charlier error with exact mean and second factorial cumulant, a uniform mean-bias bound and eventual probability status. Exact and nominal Poisson total variation have their distinct remainder powers and the same moving residue equivalent. Every fixed polynomial weight and factorial moment, the zero-count probability, and the literal integer quantization and cost of replacing the exact mean are recorded.
entries.title: P1 publication: Optimal quadratic approximation and Poisson scales

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization retaining the upper representation bounds and the conditional consequence of Duke–Schulze-Pillot (Invent. Math. 99, 1990), and adding an unconditional fixed-cap theorem for x^2+y^2+z^2. H1: for every unit vector u in R^3 and every epsilon > 0 there is T such that every squarefree t >= T with t congruent to 3 modulo 8 has an integer representation x with sum x_i^2=t and |x_i-sqrt(t)u_i| <= epsilon sqrt(t) for every coordinate. The new statement takes no analytic estimate as a hypothesis. Its proof combines finite-degree harmonic Weyl bounds, odd-degree cancellation, a positive minimum of finitely many degree-dependent savings, and a representation lower bound supplied by the verified Siegel theorem. The threshold is ineffective. The original three unconditional upper/divisor bounds and two conditional statements are retained unchanged; the latter still require hThm1 and hThm3i for general ternary forms. No unconditional general Duke–Schulze-Pillot theorem, sharp 1/175 exponent, spinor-genus lower bound or numerical cutoff is claimed.
entries.title: Duke–Schulze-Pillot bounds and squarefree three squares in fixed caps (H1)

entries.abstract: A thin wrapper that exposes, with Mathlib definitions only, the basic recolouring lemmas of edge-colouring theory proved inside PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009 (overfull-critical-graphs). vizing_adjacency_lemma (Vizing 1965): if G is of class two (its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable) and G − xy is Δ(G)-edge-colourable, then x has at least Δ − d(y) + 1 neighbours of degree Δ other than y. critical_two_maxDegree_neighbours: every vertex of a Δ-critical graph has at least two neighbours of degree Δ. multifan_lemma (Stiebitz–Scheide–Toft–Favrholdt, Theorem 2.1): for a Δ(G)-colouring of G − x y₀ of a class-two graph, a multifan at x is elementary and x is joined to every fan vertex by a path coloured with any colour free at x and any colour free at that vertex. kierstead_lemma (Kierstead 1984): a Kierstead path whose interior vertices y₂, …, y_{L−2} have degree below Δ is elementary. Partial edge colourings are symmetric functions V → V → Option (Fin k); five definitions (proper partial edge colouring, colouring of G − ab, free colour, multifan, Kierstead path). The only new proof is the corollary (from Vizing's lemma) and the translation to the colourings of the Vizing entry.
entries.title: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma and Kierstead's lemma, as a standalone module

entries.abstract: For any decidable abelian group, two four-point finite supports with one common point and identical full labelled ordered squares exist exactly when Z/4Z × Z/4Z embeds additively. The ambient group need not be cyclic or finite. No novelty assessment or independent human review is asserted.
entries.title: Singleton-overlap four-point square collisions and C4 × C4 subgroups

entries.abstract: DomainTheory is a single Lean 4 / Mathlib library (v4.36.0-rc2, lake build green, no sorry) assembled from five Palomar-registered formalizations vendored under vendor/ for provenance (scott1972, scott1976, scott1980, scott1982, scott_models; see PROVENANCE.md and vendor/FROZEN.txt). The working Lean is the golfed DomainTheory/ tree: ContinuousLattice ← 1972, DataTypesAsLattices ← 1976, NeighbourhoodSystems ← 1980, InformationSystems ← 1982, BridgeTheorems ← scott_models. Comparator (Challenge.lean / Solution.lean / comparator.json) validates (i) the cross-presentation bridges formerly registered as scott_models (1972 continuous-lattice / 1980 neighbourhood / 1982 information-system isomorphisms, including D ≃o RoundFilter ≃o RoundInfoSysElement and the S-expression equation |T| ≃o |A + (T × T)|), and (ii) the selected Data Types as Lattices (1976) declarations formerly registered as scott1976. The golfed library preserves those validated results under Mathlib-style names. Distribution today is the public GitHub repository only; a CMU-CS technical report (CMU-CS-TR) is planned. Author Contributions: Lars Warren Ericson — primary formalization engineer (all Lean 4, AI-assisted proof architecture, repository assembly); Dana S. Scott — author of the original source mathematics (1972–1982), project sponsorship, historical context, and high-level advisory oversight of formalization scope; Vijay D'Silva and Brian Milnes — project initiation, pre-submission review, and advisory feedback on repository formatting and technical report generation. Source-paper authorship is distinct from combined-library co-authorship; Scott, D'Silva, and Milnes did not write the Lean.
entries.title: DomainTheory — Scott domain theory 1972–1982 with cross-presentation bridges

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of two lower-bound constructions for the Gallai–van der Waerden numbers GW(r; k, l) of Mao, Ozeki, Robertson and Wang (the least M such that for every n ≥ M, every exact r-colouring of {1, …, n} contains a rainbow k-term or a monochromatic l-term arithmetic progression), for rainbow (m + 1)-term progressions and every m. Let p > l ≥ 2 be a prime with p ≡ 1 (mod m) such that (i) for every i in {0, …, m} the m residues j − i (j ≠ i, 0 ≤ j ≤ m) do not lie in m distinct m-th power classes modulo p, and (ii) no l consecutive integers in [1, p − 1] lie in one class. Theorem 4: colouring x in [1, (l − 1)p] by (x − 1)^((p − 1)/m) mod p (the m-th power class of x − 1, and a new colour 0 on the zero class x ≡ 1 (mod p)) uses exactly m + 1 colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term and no monochromatic l-term progression, so GW(m + 1; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p. Theorem 8: if instead the zero class 1 + kp (0 ≤ k ≤ l − 1) of [1, (l − 1)p + 1] is coloured by s ≥ 2 new colours z(k), where z uses all s colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term progression, the colouring uses exactly m + s colours and is good, so GW(m + s; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p + 1. The formalization proves both theorems for every such m, l, p (and s, z), the resulting bounds for GW (unconditionally for every threshold with the defining property, and for the number itself given that a threshold exists), and five instances with l = 4: GW(4; 4, 4) > 327, GW(5; 5, 4) > 1059, GW(6; 6, 4) > 2253, GW(6; 4, 4) > 328 and GW(8; 5, 4) > 1060.
entries.title: Gallai–van der Waerden numbers from m-th power residue colourings

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of dimension formulas for planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations and their equilibrium measures. The headline results are Theorems A, B and 4.16; Solution.lean presents the numbered statements in manuscript order.
entries.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations: Lean formalisation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the theorem of Erdős and Wilson (1977) that almost every graph is of class one: among the 2^C(n,2) labelled graphs on Fin n, the proportion whose line graph is Δ(G)-colourable tends to 1 (erdos_wilson). On the way it proves that almost every graph has a unique vertex of maximum degree (tendsto_unique_maxDegree) and that a graph with at most one vertex of maximum degree is of class one (colorable_of_subsingleton_maxDegree, the special case of Fournier's theorem imported from PALOMAR-2026-11-08-000009). The probabilistic part is a second-moment argument with explicit binomial estimates: with X the number of vertices of degree at least a threshold k, P(X = 0) ≤ 1/(n tl_k) + bp_{k-1}^2/(4 tl_k^2) and P(two distinct vertices of equal degree ≥ k) ≤ n^2 Σ_{i ≥ k-1} bp_i^2, where bp, tl are the point probabilities and upper tails of Bin(n-2, 1/2); the joint law of two degrees is computed exactly by a symmetric-difference (translation) argument on the set of graphs, and k is chosen adaptively. Only qualitative statements (limits) are stated; no rate of convergence is claimed. Three statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Erdős–Wilson: almost every graph is of class one

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on finite simple graphs G whose core (the vertices of maximum degree Δ) has maximum degree at most two, stated as: every vertex of degree Δ has at most two neighbours of degree Δ. Hilton–Zhao (1992): if G is connected and not Δ-edge-colourable, then G − e is Δ-edge-colourable for every edge e, every vertex has at least two neighbours of degree Δ (so the core is 2-regular), and every vertex has degree at least Δ − 1, with equality somewhere when Δ ≥ 3 (hiltonZhao_critical, hiltonZhao_two_le, hiltonZhao_core_regular, hiltonZhao_min_degree, hiltonZhao_min_degree_eq); corollaries: class one when some vertex of degree Δ has at most one neighbour of degree Δ, or some vertex has degree at most Δ − 2. For Δ = 3: a connected class-two graph is a petal graph (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 3: degrees 2 or 3, the degree-3 vertices induce a 2-regular graph, degree-2 vertices have only degree-3 neighbours) and 3|E| = 4|V|; and if some component of the core carries no internal petal (no vertex of degree below 3 adjacent to two of its vertices) then G is 3-edge-colourable (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 7, for a single core cycle). The graph P* (Petersen minus a vertex) is defined on Fin 9, proved isomorphic to the Petersen graph minus a vertex, and shown to satisfy the hypotheses, to be connected, of class two and not overfull. Cariolaro–Cariolaro (2003): a connected graph with Δ = 3 whose core has maximum degree at most two is not 3-edge-colourable if and only if it is isomorphic to P* (cariolaro_iff, cariolaro). The proof recolours one core cycle with its petals in a colouring of G − e (criticality): a combinatorial chorded-cycle lemma (a cyclic sequence of vertices with chords and external restrictions has a proper 3-edge-colouring whose missing colours differ along chords and avoid the restrictions, unless it is the hexagon with three antipodal chords or a chordless odd cycle with constant restrictions) proved by induction with safe local reductions; the arc reduction rests on a finite automaton whose reachable states are checked by decide. Vizing's theorem and Vizing's adjacency lemma are lake dependencies on PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009; Kempe chains and their end-point lemma come from the former.
entries.title: Graphs whose core has maximum degree two: Hilton–Zhao structure and the Cariolaro–Cariolaro theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Theorem 2 of Chetwynd and Hilton, "1-factorizing regular graphs of high degree — an improved bound" (Discrete Math. 75 (1989)): a d-regular simple graph of even order with d ≥ ½(√7 − 1)|V| (≈ 0.823|V|) is d-edge-colourable (CH89.lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular_sqrt7), with the integer form |V| = 2n, 7n² ≤ (d + n)² (CH89.lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular_nat). The article's proof of Theorem 1 contains an unjustified step ("we may moreover suppose that x_j comes before w_j in the list (r_m, …, r_t, l_1, …, l_m)"), which fails for an arbitrary maximal matching M₀; the formalization repairs it by choosing M₀ to minimize −K·#covered + max(T, T′), T = u_Y − u_X − μ, ordering the edges of M₀ (mixed ones outside, XX/YY alternately) and pairing X with Y by Hall's theorem with one dummy, so that at most one pair is bad, which the article's extra step q + 1 absorbs. The constant ½(√7 − 1) of the article is obtained exactly. Theorem 1 (staircase classes peeled off as near 1-factors, core of Theorem 5, re-insertion of v* and w) is assembled from the pinned dependency PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016; Lemma 3 (a pair with r(r − 1) ≤ (2n − 1)p common non-neighbours) and the parameter inequality r(r − 1) − (2n − 1)(5n − 3d − 1) = (d + n)² − 7n² + n + 1 are proved here. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Chetwynd–Hilton 1989: regular graphs of degree at least ½(√7 − 1)|V| are 1-factorizable

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Siegel's theorem (1935): for every ε > 0 there is c > 0 with c·N^(-ε) ≤ ‖L(1, χ)‖ for every real non-principal Dirichlet character χ modulo N (SiegelThm.siegel, with Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction; χ need not be primitive). The proof is Goldfeld's (1974): F = ζ·L(χ₁)L(χ₂)L(χ₁χ₂) has non-negative Dirichlet coefficients with a₁ = 1; its regular part G = F − λ/(s−1) is expanded in a Taylor series at s = 2, with Cauchy's estimate on the circle |s−2| = 3/2 (where |G| ≤ 4000 (N₁N₂)²), giving ‖λ‖ ≥ (1−β)/2 · (50000 (N₁N₂)²)^(−4(1−β)) whenever Re F(β) ≤ 0 and 7/8 ≤ β < 1; Siegel's dichotomy (an exceptional zero in [1−ε/16, 1) or none, in which case χ₁ is the character mod 4) gives the ineffective constant. Characters that induce the same character as χ₁ are handled with the Euler factors (∏_{p∣n}(1−1/p) ≥ c(η)n^(−η)). Two auxiliary statements are also compared: the integral representation L(s, χ) = s∫_1^∞ A(t) t^(−s−1) dt on Re s > 0 (SiegelThm.LFunction_eq_integral, via Mathlib's Abel summation for Re s > 1, a Mellin-transform holomorphy argument and the identity theorem) and ‖∑_{k≤M} χ(k)‖ ≤ N (SiegelThm.norm_sum_Icc_le). Mathlib is the only dependency; Mathlib's continuation of ζ is not used (ζ(s) = 1/(s−1) + 1 − s∫_1^∞{t}t^(−s−1) dt is proved directly). Three statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
entries.title: Siegel's theorem on L(1, χ) for real Dirichlet characters

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Lovász's (g,f)-factor theorem (1970): for a finite simple graph G and g ≤ f : V → ℕ, G has a spanning subgraph H with g(v) ≤ deg_H(v) ≤ f(v) for every vertex if and only if, for all disjoint vertex sets S and T, h(S,T) ≤ Σ_{v∈S} f(v) + Σ_{v∈T} (deg_{G−S}(v) − g(v)), where h(S,T) is the number of components C of G − (S ∪ T) with g = f on C and Σ_{v∈C} f(v) + e(C,T) odd (lovasz_gf_factor). As a corollary, the criterion of Heinrich, Hell, Kirkpatrick and Liu for g < f, without the component term (gf_factor_of_lt). The proof reduces the theorem to Tutte's f-factor theorem, imported as a lake dependency from PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000005, through a gadget: f(v) − g(v) slack vertices are joined to each vertex v, and the slack vertices together with one extra vertex form a clique, with target degree 1 on slack vertices and (Σ g) mod 2 on the extra vertex. One definition beyond Mathlib's (h(S,T), tightOddCount); g and f are natural-number valued.
entries.title: Lovász's (g,f)-factor theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of a lower-bound construction for the Gallai–van der Waerden numbers GW(r; 3, l) of Mao, Ozeki, Robertson and Wang: the least m such that for every n ≥ m, every exact r-colouring of {1, …, n} contains a rainbow 3-term or a monochromatic l-term arithmetic progression. Theorem 1: let l ≥ 4 and let p > l be a prime with p ≡ 1 (mod 8) such that no l consecutive integers in [1, p − 1] have the same Legendre symbol modulo p; let s ≥ 2 and let z colour {0, …, l − 1} onto s colours with no rainbow 3-term progression. Colour x in [1, (l − 1)p + 1] by its quadratic character of x − 1 (two colours) when x ≢ 1 (mod p), and the point x = 1 + kp by the new colour 2 + z(k). This colouring uses all s + 2 colours and has no rainbow 3-term and no monochromatic l-term progression, so GW(s + 2; 3, l) > (l − 1)p + 1. The formalization proves Theorem 1 for every such l, p, s and z, the resulting bound for GW (unconditionally for every threshold with the defining property, and for the number itself given that a threshold exists), and the instance (l, p) = (4, 17), which gives GW(4; 3, 4) > 52 and GW(5; 3, 4) > 52.
entries.title: Gallai–van der Waerden numbers from quadratic-residue colourings

entries.abstract: There is a countable group G such that the Bernoulli shifts of G with bases (L, lambda) and (L', lambda') are isomorphic for all standard probability spaces whose measures are not point masses: there is an equivariant, measure-preserving bijection, measurable in both directions, between shift-invariant measurable sets of full measure. No condition is put on the entropies of the bases, which may differ and may be infinite. The group is N x (Z/2 wr Z), where N is the group of the pinned OpenAI construction, which supplies the algebraic existence input. This formalization does not certify finitary or continuous conjugacy and says nothing about other groups.
entries.title: A countable group all of whose nontrivial Bernoulli shifts are isomorphic

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. An additive map phi between associative rings is a Jordan homomorphism when phi(ab + ba) = phi(a)phi(b) + phi(b)phi(a). (1) A Jordan homomorphism onto a prime ring without 2-torsion is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism (phi(ab) = phi(b)phi(a)): Herstein's theorem (1956, Theorem H) in the form Smiley gave it (1957, p. 428), with characteristic 3 admitted; an additive map of rings, no identity assumed. (2) The domain form in every characteristic (Jacobson and Rickart 1950, Theorem 2): an additive map with phi(a^2) = phi(a)^2 and phi(aba) = phi(a)phi(b)phi(a), into a ring without zero divisors, is multiplicative or anti-multiplicative, with no surjectivity and no hypothesis on 2. (3)-(5) Each hypothesis of (1) is needed; each statement asserts that one hypothesis fails, that the others hold, and that the map is neither multiplicative nor anti-multiplicative: (3) from 2x2 into 4x4 integer matrices, not onto, the target prime and without 2-torsion (witness a -> diag(a, a^T)); (4) on pairs of 2x2 integer matrices, onto, the target not prime (witness (a, b) -> (a, b^T)); (5) from F_2 x F_2 onto F_2, a prime ring with 2-torsion (witness (x, y) -> x + y). (6) The theorem in every characteristic (Smiley 1957, Added in proof, p. 429): an additive map with the two identities of (2), onto a prime ring, is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with no hypothesis on 2; it implies (1), and (5) shows that the Jordan identity alone does not suffice when the ring has 2-torsion. The compared statements add no definition: the identities on the map and the conditions on the target ring are written out as universally quantified statements, the maps are Mathlib's AddMonoidHom, and onto is Function.Surjective. Statements 1, 2 and 6 formalize theorems of the 1950s and statements 3-5 are standard examples; nothing here is a new theorem. The proof of (1) follows the argument written out by Beidar, Bresar and Chebotar (2003, Proposition 3.1), not Smiley's; the proof of (2) is Jacobson and Rickart's; the proof of (6) is Smiley's, through his lemma that a prime ring in which every commutator squares to zero is commutative. Not formalized: the semiprime generalizations. A prior formalization of the case of complex-linear maps between unital complex algebras exists in github.com/openai/math and is recorded under related_formalizations; statements (1) and (6) contain that case. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): the self-adjoint elements of an algebra of observables are closed under the symmetrized product and not, in general, under the product; applied to the identity map, (1) says that on a prime ring without 2-torsion the symmetrized product determines the associative product up to reversing the order of the factors.
entries.title: Herstein's theorem on Jordan homomorphisms onto prime rings, in Smiley's form for characteristic different from 2 and in his form for every characteristic, with the Jacobson-Rickart domain theorem and an example for each hypothesis

entries.abstract: For a metric continuum X, D(X) is the hyperspace of subcontinua of X that are the closure of their interior, with the Hausdorff metric. The project formalizes the theorem that a countable D(X) is a G-delta subset of the hyperspace of subcontinua, hence completely metrizable and scattered with dense isolated points, so that D(X) is never homeomorphic to the rationals; together with the structure theory behind it (independent families, blister theorem, complement lemma, absorption by minimal elements, decreasing intersections, density of minimal elements, D-atomic continua, the cardinality dichotomy).
entries.title: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua

entries.abstract: Formal Lean 4 fixed-quarter Brun–Titchmarsh-type estimate for nonnegative multiplicative weights without squarefree support, with a separate fixed B*n^(1/1280) growth witness. Includes the ordinary modulus-one short-interval corollary with a factor of nine in the bound, and a uniform upper-right parameter-quadrant consequence 1/4 <= alpha,beta < 1/2.
entries.title: Shiu Bounds Toolkit

entries.abstract: A general theorem and its six instances. The theorem (congr_of): let k = 12 + 4a + 6b; if the space M_{k−12} of level-one modular forms has rank one and 2k/B_k = D/ℓ with ℓ and D coprime integers, then the q-expansion coefficients of Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b are integers congruent to σ_{k−1}(n) modulo ℓ, for every n. The hypothesis holds exactly for k = 12, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26, where the cusp space is spanned by this one form, and the instances are the congruences modulo the numerator of B_k/2k: 691, 3617, 43867, 174611 = 283·617, 77683 = 131·593 and 657931. The case k = 12 is Ramanujan's τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) (mod 691); the other five are the remaining congruences of this kind at level one. The statements are for every n and use only Mathlib definitions; the Bernoulli numbers B_12 to B_26 are computed in Lean, not assumed. Integrality comes from the product formula for Δ, expanded by Mathlib's pentagonal number theorem, and the integer coefficients 240σ₃ and −504σ₅ of E₄ and E₆. The congruence comes from one exact identity in M_k: E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k vanishes at the cusp, so dividing by Δ (Mathlib's discriminantEquiv) gives a form in M_{k−12}, which is one-dimensional and spanned by E₄^a·E₆^b; hence E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k = c·Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b, with c read off from the q¹-coefficient. Since E_k = 1 − (2k/B_k)∑σ_{k−1}(n)qⁿ, multiplying by the numerator of B_k/2k and reducing shows that the Eisenstein series is congruent to the cusp form. The argument is proved once for general (a, b) and applied to the six cases.
entries.title: Ramanujan's congruences for the one-dimensional cusp spaces

entries.abstract: For a nonempty finite set of integers excluding 0, 1, and −1, consider the primes for which every integer in the set is a primitive root. When neither Matthews obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes have a lower bound of order x/log x in every sufficiently large real dyadic interval (x, 2x] and positive lower relative density among the primes. When either obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes form a finite set. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper.
entries.title: An Unconditional Artin–Matthews Theorem for Simultaneous Primitive Roots

entries.abstract: This submission strengthens PALOMAR-2026-11-09-000019 and is proposed as the next version of that existing registration, using the same repository and Comparator configuration path. Version 1 states that no proper principal upper cone of the ordinary Turing degrees is order-isomorphic to the whole degree structure. This revision proves that two principal upper cones are order-isomorphic if and only if their base degrees are equal, and that every such isomorphism fixes every underlying degree. Consequently, every individual cone has only the identity automorphism. Both compared statements concern arbitrary order isomorphisms, without regularity, determinacy, persistence, or model-existence hypotheses. The earlier theorem remains valid as a special case; this is a substantive strengthening, not a correction or retraction of version 1, whose record and archived source remain unchanged.
entries.title: Pairwise rigidity of principal upper cones of Turing degrees

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that f(n, k), the least number such that the edges of every graph with n vertices and k edges can be partitioned into at most f(n, k) cliques, satisfies f(n, k) = n² B(k/n²) + o(n²) uniformly in 0 ≤ k ≤ n(n − 1)/2, for an explicit continuous piecewise-algebraic function B on [0, 1/2]. B(d) = d for d ≤ 1/4; above 1/4 it is the larger of two curves built from explicit dual certificates on split, mixed and two-head graphs. This provides an asymptotic resolution of Erdős Problem 1017, as posed by Erdős and as stated by Bloom, who asks for an estimate of f(n, k) for k > n²/4. The formula is new to our knowledge. The proof passes through the fractional relaxation and proves again, in Lean, the case of the fractional-to-integral transfer of Balogh, He, Krueger, Nguyen and Wigal that it needs.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 1017: clique partitions of graphs of given size

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.
entries.title: Stafford 3.8

entries.abstract: For every natural N there is n at least N and an n-point set in the single fixed Euclidean space R^29 whose distances on different unordered pairs of distinct points differ by at least one, with diameter strictly below (499/500)n^2. The sizes n form an unbounded set; no claim is made for every large n. As a consequence the formalization proves the negation of the fixed-dimension proposition for Erdős Problem 670 exactly as stated in Formal Conjectures at commit 2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf, using d = 29 and epsilon = 1/1000. No optimality, smallest dimension or independent priority review is claimed.
entries.title: Separated distances in the fixed space R^29

entries.abstract: Let f(y) be the decimal reversal of the y-th prime (f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3, f(5) = 11, f(11) = 13). OEIS A100475 is the orbit of 1 under f, and its entry asks (Jonathan Vos Post, 2004) whether the orbit of any other positive start ever enters a loop. This project proves that it never does, i.e. the negation of the formal-conjectures statement OeisA100475.conjecture: the number of digits never decreases along an orbit (p_y > y, and a prime never ends in 0), so on a cycle it is a constant D and every cycle element v satisfies p_v < 10^D; for D <= 4 this forces v <= 1229, and a kernel-checked table of the first 1230 primes with an escape-time ranking shows that no cycle stays below 1230; for D >= 5 it contradicts the bound pi'(10^D) < 10^(D-1) on the number of primes below 10^D, proved for D = 5, ..., 8 by Legendre's sieve recursion evaluated by the Lean kernel and for D >= 9 by Chebyshev's bound theta(x) <= x log 4 with the split point 10^(D-2).
entries.title: OEIS A100475: the reverse-prime map never loops

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of Theorems A–F for absorbing Markov chains on compact metric spaces under Hypothesis H. The results give conditional Poisson point-process and shrinking-target limits, stable laws and their Gaussian boundary, an L2 central limit theorem, exponential concentration, and conditional laws of large numbers. The registry statement exposes the canonical path laws, local admissibility, and normalised spectral data; existence of the spectral data is proved from H.
entries.title: Conditional stable laws and rare-event limits for absorbing Markov chains

entries.abstract: For every n >= 4 the Cayley graph of S_n with unit-cost generators L = (0 1 ... n-1), R = L inverse, and X = (0 1) has diameter n*(n-1)/2. The formalization proves upper and lower bounds and a literal L/R/X word of at most that length between every ordered pair of permutations. The independent Challenge defines the moves, their word evaluation, and the undirected Cayley graph using Mathlib alone.
entries.title: Exact LRX diameter of the symmetric group

entries.abstract: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability theorem is also proved: if the neighbour count of every unchosen vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every *proper common MCS prefix* (the sets the constructive proof actually visits -- a hypothesis strictly weaker than the every-subset bound, which is equivalent to adding a matching), the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering. This strengthening (exists_common_ordering_prefix) makes the matching result a genuine corollary; the every-subset version exists_common_ordering is retained as a special case.
entries.title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance

entries.abstract: For 1/2 ≤ θ < 1, the Riemann zeta function has no zeros with real part greater than θ if and only if Chebyshev's ψ(x) = x + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequences: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+δ}) for all δ > 0, and the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis) yields ψ(x) = x + O(x^{7/8+δ}). Both directions are proved: the easy direction by partial summation and holomorphy of a Mellin transform; the hard direction by a smoothed Chebyshev function, a contour shift to a vertical line inside the zero-free half-plane, and a bound ζ'/ζ(σ+it) ≪ log|t| obtained from the Borel–Carathéodory theorem.
entries.title: Ingham's theorem: zero-free half-planes of the Riemann zeta function and the error term in the prime number theorem

entries.abstract: Let M be the n x n matrix with entries 1/lcm(i,j). R. G. Wilson v conjectured (OEIS A060841, 2015) that 1/det(M) is an integer only for n = 1, ..., 34, 36 and 38. This project proves the conjecture as stated in formal-conjectures (OeisA60841.conjecture1): by Smith's determinant the gcd matrix factors as E diag(phi) E^T with E the unitriangular divisibility matrix, so 1/det(M) = (n!)^2 / prod_{k <= n} phi(k); for n in {1, ..., 34, 36, 38} the divisibility is decided by computation, and for every other n the odd primes up to 97 and the powers of 2 from 4 to 128 force v_2(prod phi(k)) > v_2((n!)^2), numerically for n = 35, 37 and 39 <= n < 100 and by a linear bound for n >= 100.
entries.title: OEIS A060841: 1/det(1/lcm(i,j)) is an integer exactly for n <= 34, n = 36 and n = 38

entries.abstract: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Ideal Generation for General Reduced Projective Points. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, for every projective dimension n >= 1, degree D >= 2 and point count between binomial(n+D-1,D-1) and binomial(n+D,D)-1, a nonempty principal open of ordered reduced point configurations has maximal-rank multiplication from I_D tensor S_1 to I_(D+1). The homogeneous ideal has the exact predicted numbers of minimal generators in degrees D and D+1 and is generated in those degrees. Generality is expressed in the standard affine chart of projective space. The points are actual projective classes and their homogeneous ideal is radical.
entries.title: Ideal generation for general reduced projective points

entries.abstract: A general Carleson theorem for doubling measure metric spaces, implying Carleson's classical theorem about pointwise a.e. convergence of Fourier series for continuous periodic functions on the real line
entries.title: Carleson

entries.abstract: For a metric continuum X, a subcontinuum is regular if it equals the closure of its interior, and D(X) denotes the hyperspace of regular subcontinua with the Hausdorff metric. Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez asked whether D(X) can be homeomorphic to the rationals or to the irrationals. This project formalizes in Lean 4 with Mathlib the complete proof of the affirmative answer for the irrationals: there is a nondegenerate compact connected set X in the Hilbert space ℓ² such that D(X) is homeomorphic to the Baire space ℕ^ℕ and to the space of irrational numbers. The continuum X is the closure of a countable tree of scaled copies of the Knaster continuum, realized in ℓ² as the inverse limit of the tent map. The formalization proves that the regular subcontinua of X are coded exactly by the nonempty, convex sets of pieces that satisfy a density condition. It shows that this coding is a homeomorphism onto a nonempty, zero-dimensional G_δ subset of a Cantor cube in which every compact set has empty interior. It then concludes with the Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of the Baire space and the homeomorphism between ℕ^ℕ and the irrationals. Both classical results are also proved in the project.
entries.title: A continuum whose hyperspace of regular subcontinua is homeomorphic to the irrationals

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every Lebesgue measurable subset of the plane with positive upper Banach density contains a translated and rotated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle. The proof was developed using GPT 6 Astra Pro. The Lean formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.
entries.title: Triangles in sets of positive upper density in the plane

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of three existence theorems for discounted stationary first-order mean-field games in positive dimension. Under the paper's monotonicity and respective growth hypotheses, the results give strong solutions for standard power growth and singular congestion, and weak solutions for weak growth. Each result includes density integrability, Sobolev regularity, nonnegativity, identification of the returned weak gradient, and its integrability. The congestion result permits infinite Hamiltonian limits at zero mass and a general continuous limiting flux; the weak-growth result imposes no boundary condition on the original Hamiltonian. The independent Challenge contains the definitions and statements; Solution connects them to the included proof development.
entries.title: Existence of stationary mean-field games by monotonicity methods

entries.abstract: Let N >= 2 be an integer, let u_1 < u_2 < ... be positive integers with liminf u_{j+1}/u_j >= 2, and let lambda_j be nonzero rational numbers with log H(lambda_j) = o(u_j), where H(a/b) = max(|a|, b) in lowest terms. The series x = sum_j lambda_j N^{-u_j} converges absolutely, is irrational, and has irrationality exponent limsup u_{j+1}/u_j, finite or infinite. The coefficients may have arbitrary signs, and the boundary case liminf u_{j+1}/u_j = 2 is included, with ratios allowed to approach 2 from below. The proof compares continued-fraction denominator gaps of consecutive truncations. A perturbation lemma places each new gap in at least one of five classes: bounded, inherited, central, short, or reflected. The reflected class gives the estimate needed at the boundary ratio 2. This project formalizes the paper's main theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: The irrationality exponent of small-height lacunary series

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem in every finite dimension: a continuous map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space into itself has a fixed point. Also proved: the same for closed balls of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and the no-retraction theorem, that the unit sphere of such a space is not a retract of its closed unit ball.

The proof is analytic, along the lines of Milnor (1978) and Rogers (1980), and uses no homology, degree theory or simplicial approximation. A C1 retraction r of the closed unit ball onto its sphere is ruled out with the change of variables formula: for small t > 0 the map x + t(r(x) - x) sends the open ball bijectively onto itself with positive Jacobian determinant, so the integral of that determinant over the ball, a polynomial in t, equals the volume of the ball for every t, whereas at t = 1 it vanishes. Brouwer's theorem follows for C1 self-maps of the ball by the ray construction, for continuous ones by smoothing by convolution, and for compact convex sets through the nearest-point retraction. Brouwer's theorem has earlier formal proofs in HOL Light, Isabelle/HOL and Mizar, in Coq for the plane, in Lean 3 through singular homology, and in Lean 4 for the plane and for the standard simplex; this proof is independent of them. A second proof follows Knaster, Kuratowski and Mazurkiewicz (1929): Sperner's lemma for the iterated barycentric subdivisions of the simplex, by counting facets mod 2, then the KKM lemma and Brouwer's theorem for the simplex; Kakutani's and Schauder's proofs use this one, the proof of Brouwer's theorem that both papers cite.

Kakutani's fixed-point theorem (1941) and Schauder's fixed-point theorem (1930) are derived from Brouwer's.
